feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (12 mm footprint, y=0.05, 0.6 kg, baseline controller) is the only stable design, finishing the oval 20/20 in 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15 but failing the s-bend at 0.17 and the slalom at 0.12 with max_error near 0.061 m. Iterations 3 and 4 showed that moving the sensor row to y=0.07 or y=0.03 collapsed the oval to 0/20, so y=0.05 should stay fixed for any further test. Iterations 1 and 2 showed that the 0.5 kg mass and the wide array both cost oval finishes, and the bend gain from the wider array was small (0.17 to 0.24). I kept the controller at baseline so only the footprint changes. Next race: if the oval holds at 19/20 or better near 1.65 s and bend progress rises above 0.17 and 0.12, keep the 8 mm footprint and test a modest spread increase at 0.6 kg. If the oval drops or steering oscillation rises above about 0.2, return to 12 mm and test a 16 mm footprint at the same spread. If bend progress is unchanged with max_error still near 0.06, the footprint is not the bend limit, so the next test should change spread alone.
requested_changes: If the oval finishes at least 19/20 near 1.65 s and s-bend or slalom progress rises above 0.17 or 0.12, keep sensor_size 0.008 and widen sensor x to plus or minus 0.028 m (pitch 14 mm) with mass held at 0.6 kg, since iteration 1 gave a partial bend gain from the wider array.

If the oval falls below 19/20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 (baseline 0.15), return sensor_size to 0.012 and test sensor_size 0.016 at x plus or minus 0.024 and y 0.05, since iteration 0 showed the bends fail at max_error 0.061 with a 12 mm footprint.
Keep sensor y at 0.05 m for every next test, since iteration 3 (y=0.07) and iteration 4 (y=0.03) both collapsed the oval to 0/20 while the baseline at y=0.05 finished 20/20.
